questions.q: What base class does every LWC component's JavaScript class extend?
options: HTMLElement, directly, with no Salesforce-specific base class
LightningElement, imported from the built-in `lwc` module
AuraComponent, imported from the `aura` module
WebComponent, imported from `@salesforce/lwc`
questions.explain: Every LWC component class extends `LightningElement`, imported from the `lwc` module. `LightningElement` itself is built on the browser's native `HTMLElement`, but components extend `LightningElement` directly, not `HTMLElement`.

questions.q: If a component defines a `constructor()`, what must be true about it?
options: It must call `this.template.querySelector` before anything else
It must call `super()` as its very first statement
It must return a Promise
It must be marked with the `@api` decorator
questions.explain: Calling `super()` as the first statement in a constructor is a general JavaScript rule for any class extending another class, and it applies to LWC components the same as any other class.

questions.q: Why is it unsafe to call `this.template.querySelector(...)` inside a component's constructor?
options: Because `querySelector` is not a real browser method
Because the constructor runs before the component is connected to the DOM, so nothing is rendered yet to query
Because `this.template` is only available inside `@api` properties
Because constructors in LWC are executed on the server, not the browser
questions.explain: The constructor runs before the component is connected to the DOM. Since nothing has rendered yet at that point, there's no rendered DOM for `this.template.querySelector` to find anything in.

questions.q: What actually causes an LWC template to re-render when a tracked field changes?
options: Calling a `render()` method explicitly, similar to some other UI frameworks
Calling a `setState()` method on the component instance
Simple assignment to the field (e.g. `this.isEditing = true;`) -- the framework automatically re-renders anything depending on that field
Re-running the component's constructor
questions.explain: LWC doesn't require a manual render or setState call. Plain assignment to a field the template depends on is enough -- the framework automatically tracks the dependency and re-renders what needs to change.

questions.q: How does a component's `.js` file get connected to its `.html` template file?
options: Through an explicit `import` statement inside the HTML file that references the JS class
Through a registration call made inside the `js-meta.xml` file
Automatically, because the `.js` and `.html` files in the same bundle share the same component name by convention
They are never directly connected; data passes between them only through Apex
questions.explain: The framework connects a bundle's `.js` and `.html` files automatically based on them sharing the same component name -- there's no manual import or registration step linking the two.
